glosses.notes: Means to accompany someone in an official, practical, or supportive way through a visit, trip, or task.

examples.sentence: 医生说老人今天要再做一次检查，所以女儿一早就请了假陪同他过去，免得中间有哪一步听不清楚。
领导没有让他一个人去谈，而是安排一位更有经验的人陪同，这样真有问题也能当场说清楚。
记者进现场以前都得有人陪同，不是怕他们乱看，而是有些地方现在还不能随便进去。

example_translations.translation: The doctor said that the elderly man needed another examination today, so his daughter took leave early in the morning to accompany him there, in case there was some step in the middle that he could not hear clearly.
The manager did not let him go talk alone, but instead arranged for a more experienced person to accompany him, so that if a problem really came up it could be explained clearly on the spot.
Before reporters enter the site, someone has to accompany them. It is not because people are afraid they will look around randomly, but because some areas still cannot be entered casually right now.

glosses.notes: To cultivate or nurture, often for plants, habits, talent, values, or future ability.

examples.sentence: 这种树不是种下去就行，真正难的是后面怎么培育，不然后面花的时间很快就白费了。
老师说教育孩子不像做题，不能只看今天有没有结果，更要看平时怎么慢慢培育他的习惯。
这个地方这些年一直在培育新的技术人才，所以很多年轻人毕业以后不用再急着往外走。

example_translations.translation: With this kind of tree, it is not enough simply to plant it. What is truly difficult is how to cultivate it afterward, otherwise the time spent later is quickly wasted.

The teacher said that educating children is not like doing problems. You cannot look only at whether there is a result today; you have to look even more at how their habits are slowly cultivated in ordinary times.
This place has been cultivating new technical talent for these past years, so many young people no longer need to hurry to leave after graduation.

glosses.notes: Can mean to equip, allocate what is needed, or refer to the equipment and supporting items themselves.

examples.sentence: 这家医院虽然不大，但是基本的设备配备得很齐，所以来看病的人有小问题时一般都会先来这里。
学校给每个教室都重新配备了新电脑，不是为了好看，而是旧机器一开就慢，已经影响上课。
真正好的配备不只是买得贵，还要看是不是有人会用，出了问题能不能及时修。

example_translations.translation: Although this hospital is not large, its basic equipment is very complete, so people coming to see a doctor usually come here first when they have small problems.
The school re-equipped every classroom with new computers, not for appearance, but because the old machines became slow as soon as they were turned on and were already affecting classes.
Truly good equipment is not only about buying expensive things. You also have to see whether anyone knows how to use them and whether problems can be repaired in time.

glosses.notes: To admire or feel genuine respect for someone because of their ability, attitude, or conduct.

examples.sentence: 我最佩服他的一点，不是他说得多好，而是出了这么大的问题以后，他还是能先把大家安静下来。
大家都很佩服那位老师，因为他从来不拿自己的经验压人，而是先听别人把困难说完。
她后来愿意公开讲那段失败的经历，这件事让很多原来不认识她的人也开始佩服她。

example_translations.translation: What I admire most about him is not how well he speaks, but that even after such a big problem appeared, he could still calm everyone down first.
Everyone admires that teacher, because he never uses his own experience to press others down, but first listens to other people finish describing their difficulties.
Later she became willing to speak publicly about that failed experience, and this made many people who had not known her before begin to admire her too.

glosses.notes: To form a complete set or to provide matching support so related parts work together.

examples.sentence: 这个新区看上去建得很快，可是真正能不能住得方便，还得看学校、医院和车是不是一起配套。
公司把新系统上线得很快，可是后面的培训没有配套，所以很多人明明坐在电脑前，也不知道第一步该怎么做。
父亲常说，买东西不要只看眼前便宜不便宜，还要看后面的服务是不是配套，不然以后更麻烦。

example_translations.translation: This new district seems to have been built quickly, but whether it can truly be lived in conveniently still depends on whether schools, hospitals, and transportation are all provided as a complete set.

The company put the new system online very quickly, but the later training did not match it, so many people, even while sitting in front of their computers, still did not know what the first step should be.

My father often says that when buying things, you should not look only at whether they seem cheap at the moment. You should also look at whether the later service is properly matched, otherwise it becomes even more troublesome later.

glosses.notes: To spray, spurt, or shoot outward, often for water, oil, paint, or similar substances.

examples.sentence: 工人先在墙上喷了一层水，才开始动手，因为天气太干，直接做的话很容易出问题。
孩子一按那个瓶子，水就往外喷，所以母亲马上叫他停下，免得把桌子上的纸全弄湿。
锅里刚开的时候，热油一直往外喷，父亲怕我站得太近，就让我先退到门口去。

example_translations.translation: The worker first sprayed a layer of water onto the wall before starting, because the weather was too dry and doing it directly would easily cause problems.
The moment the child pressed that bottle, water sprayed outward, so his mother immediately told him to stop, in case all the papers on the table got soaked.
When the pot had just begun boiling, the hot oil kept spurting outward. My father was afraid I was standing too close, so he told me to step back to the doorway first.

glosses.notes: To hold something up with both hands or palms, often carefully, respectfully, or protectively.

examples.sentence: 她双手捧着那只刚洗好的碗，走得很慢，因为地上还有一点水，她怕自己一不小心就掉了。
老人把那张旧照片一直捧在手里看了很久，到最后也没有说一句话，只是一直低着头。
孩子捧着老师给的小奖品回家，一进门就先放到桌子上，因为他想等父亲回来以后第一个看到。

example_translations.translation: She held the freshly washed bowl in both hands and walked very slowly, because there was still a little water on the ground and she was afraid she might drop it by accident.
The old man kept holding that old photo in his hands and looking at it for a long time. In the end he did not say a single word, and only kept his head lowered.

The child carried home the small prize the teacher had given him in both hands. As soon as he came in, he placed it on the table first, because he wanted his father to be the first to see it after coming back.

glosses.notes: To collide physically, or figuratively for ideas, interests, or positions to clash directly.

examples.sentence: 两种完全不同的想法一碰到一起，难免会有碰撞，可是真正重要的是大家能不能继续把话谈下去。
车在路口发生碰撞以后，后面的路一下全堵住了，所以很多人明明离公司不远，也迟到了很久。
年轻人的想法和老一代人的经验有时候会碰撞，可是如果谁都不肯先听，最后只会越说越远。

example_translations.translation: When two completely different ideas meet together, some collision is hard to avoid, but what really matters is whether everyone can continue talking the matter through.
After cars collided at the intersection, the road behind them was suddenly completely blocked, so many people, though not far from the company, were late for a long time.

The ideas of young people and the experience of the older generation sometimes clash, but if no one is willing to listen first, then in the end people only drift farther and farther apart in what they say.

glosses.notes: To drape, throw, or spread something over a body, surface, or scene.

examples.sentence: 夜里风大，母亲怕我出来以后着凉，就先把一件外套披在我身上，才让我跟她一起下楼。
他进门的时候还披着那件旧衣服，看得出来刚才走得很急，连先坐一下都没有，就又出去找人了。
那面山一直披着很薄的一层雾，所以车往前开的时候，大家都不敢让速度太快。

example_translations.translation: The wind was strong at night, and my mother was afraid I would catch cold after coming out, so she first draped a coat over me before letting me go downstairs with her.

When he came in, he still had that old piece of clothing draped over him. You could tell he had been walking in a hurry just now; he had not even sat down for a moment before going back out to look for someone.
That mountain was always draped in a very thin layer of mist, so while the car moved forward, no one dared let the speed get too fast.

glosses.notes: Can mean skin or leather, referring to the outer layer of a body, fruit, material, or object.

examples.sentence: 这种水果的皮看上去不太好看，可是真的切开以后，里面反而比一般的更甜一点。
这双鞋外面的皮虽然旧了，可是里面还很舒服，所以父亲一直舍不得马上换掉。
医生看了看孩子手上的皮，先说问题不大，只要这几天别再碰那个地方，慢慢就会好。

example_translations.translation: The skin of this fruit does not look especially nice, but once it is really cut open, the inside is actually a little sweeter than ordinary ones.
Although the outer leather of these shoes has become old, the inside is still comfortable, so my father has never been willing to replace them right away.
The doctor took a look at the skin on the child’s hand and first said the problem was not serious. As long as that place was not touched again over the next few days, it would gradually get better.

glosses.notes: Tired or fatigued, especially from overwork, lack of rest, or long concentration.

examples.sentence: 连着几天都睡不好，人很容易疲劳，所以医生先让他回去休息，不要急着把所有事一次做完。
开长车最怕的不是路远，而是人已经疲劳了却还觉得自己可以坚持，这样反而更危险。
她最近一直觉得眼睛很累，后来检查才知道，不只是工作太多，也和长期疲劳没有及时休息有关。

example_translations.translation: If you do not sleep well for several days in a row, you become tired very easily, so the doctor first told him to go back and rest and not hurry to finish everything at once.
What people fear most when driving a long distance is not that the road is far, but that they are already fatigued and still feel they can keep going, because that is actually more dangerous.

She had recently kept feeling that her eyes were very tired. Later an examination showed that it was not only because there was too much work, but also because of long-term fatigue without timely rest.

glosses.notes: A very short moment, pause, or span of time.

examples.sentence: 大家刚才还很吵，可是老师一开口，片刻之间就都安静下来了，连后排的人也不再说话。
他拿着那封信站在门口片刻没有动，因为里面写的内容和他原来想的完全不一样。
母亲听完那个消息以后，片刻没有说话，后来才慢慢问了一句，现在最需要我们做什么。

example_translations.translation: Everyone had been noisy just a moment before, but as soon as the teacher opened his mouth, everyone became quiet within moments, and even the people in the back row stopped talking.
He stood at the doorway holding that letter and did not move for a short moment, because what was written inside was completely different from what he had originally imagined.
After hearing that news, my mother said nothing for a brief moment, and only later slowly asked what we most needed to do now.

glosses.notes: One-sided or incomplete, usually because only one angle or part of a matter is being considered.

examples.sentence: 只看一次结果就下判断，其实很片面，因为很多真正重要的变化，往往要过一段时间才看得出来。
他把问题说得太片面了，好像只要多花一点钱就能解决，可是真正难的地方他一点也没有提到。
老师提醒我们，新闻看得太少容易片面，可是只听一种声音同样会让人越想越窄。

example_translations.translation: Making a judgment after seeing only one result is actually one-sided, because many truly important changes can usually be seen only after some time has passed.
He described the problem too one-sidedly, as if spending just a little more money could solve it, while he did not mention the truly difficult part at all.
The teacher reminded us that watching too little news easily leads to a one-sided view, but listening to only one voice can equally make a person’s thinking narrower and narrower.

glosses.notes: A swindler or scammer who cheats people by pretending to be trustworthy.

examples.sentence: 老人接到那种电话的时候，最怕的不是听不懂，而是一下着急起来，就忘了先想对方是不是骗子。
他后来才知道对方是骗子，所以那几天一直不敢告诉家里，因为钱已经转出去了。
现在很多骗子说话都很像真的工作人员，所以母亲每次接到奇怪电话，都会先挂掉再问我们。

example_translations.translation: When elderly people receive that kind of phone call, what they fear most is not failing to understand it, but becoming anxious all at once and forgetting to first think whether the other side is a swindler.
Only later did he realize that the other side was a swindler, so for those few days he did not dare tell his family, because the money had already been transferred out.
Now many swindlers speak very much like real staff members, so every time my mother receives a strange call, she hangs up first and then asks us.

glosses.notes: To float, wave, or drift lightly through the air, often for smoke, smell, sound, or cloth.

examples.sentence: 秋天一到，院子里总有一点香味慢慢飘出来，所以还没有走到门口的人也知道花开了。
她披着那条很轻的围巾站在风里，围巾一直在身后飘，看上去比平时更安静一些。
电视里那一点音乐一飘出来，父亲就不说话了，因为他一下想起了很多年轻时候的事。

example_translations.translation: As soon as autumn arrives, there is always a bit of fragrance slowly floating out in the yard, so even people who have not yet walked to the doorway know that the flowers have opened.
She stood in the wind wearing that very light scarf draped over her, and the scarf kept floating behind her, making her look quieter than usual.
The moment that bit of music drifted out from the television, my father stopped talking, because all at once he remembered many things from his youth.

glosses.notes: To drift or float along, especially on water or without strong control over direction.

examples.sentence: 雨下了一夜以后，河上漂着很多从上面冲下来的东西，所以大家一早就去看是不是桥那边出了问题。
那张纸船刚放进水里就慢慢漂远了，孩子站在边上看了很久，还想再做一个更大的试试。
如果人在海上一直没有方向地漂，再有经验也会越来越紧张，因为你根本不知道什么时候能回去。

example_translations.translation: After it rained all night, many things washed down from above were drifting on the river, so everyone went early in the morning to see whether something had happened near the bridge.
That paper boat drifted far away slowly as soon as it was set into the water. The child stood by the side looking at it for a long time and still wanted to make a larger one and try again.
If a person keeps drifting at sea without direction, then even someone with experience becomes more and more tense, because you simply do not know when you will be able to return.

glosses.notes: A channel on television, radio, or another media system carrying a certain kind of content.

examples.sentence: 父亲每天晚上都会看那个频道，不是因为里面的节目最好看，而是他已经习惯听那个主持人说话的方式。
这个频道最近一直在谈年轻人找工作的事，所以很多原来不看电视的人也开始注意它了。
孩子找了半天频道，最后还是回到原来那个，因为他只想看轻松一点的节目，不想听大人讲话。

example_translations.translation: My father watches that channel every evening, not because the programs on it are the best, but because he is already used to the way that host speaks.
This channel has recently kept discussing the topic of young people looking for work, so many people who did not originally watch television have begun paying attention to it too.
The child searched through channels for a long time, but in the end still returned to the original one, because he only wanted to watch a lighter program and did not want to listen to adults talking.

glosses.notes: Frequent, happening often and repeatedly over a period of time.

examples.sentence: 如果一个系统最近频繁出问题，最需要做的不是先安慰大家，而是马上找出到底是哪一步不对。
他这段时间频繁请假，不是因为不想来上班，而是家里老人身体一直反复，实在离不开人。
两个人如果频繁因为小事吵起来，往往不是事情本身太大，而是前面很多话都没有好好说清楚。

example_translations.translation: If a system has been having problems frequently recently, what most needs to be done is not to comfort everyone first, but to immediately find out which step is actually wrong.

He has been taking leave frequently during this period, not because he does not want to come to work, but because the elderly person at home has kept getting unwell again and again, and truly cannot be left without someone.
If two people frequently start arguing because of small matters, then usually it is not because the matter itself is too big, but because many things earlier were never explained clearly.

glosses.notes: Poor or impoverished, usually describing difficult economic living conditions.

examples.sentence: 他小时候家里很贫困，所以长大以后花钱一直很小心，哪怕现在生活已经比以前好了很多。
这个地方以前一直比较贫困，后来路通了、学校也多了，很多孩子才开始看到别的可能。
老师说，帮助贫困家庭的孩子，不只是给他们一点东西，更重要的是让他们以后有更多路可以走。

example_translations.translation: His family was very poor when he was young, so after growing up he has always been very careful with money, even though life is much better now than before.
This place used to be rather impoverished, but later the roads opened and the number of schools increased, and only then did many children begin to see other possibilities.
The teacher said that helping children from poor families is not only about giving them a few things, but more importantly about letting them have more roads open to them later.

glosses.notes: Frequency, how often something happens or repeats within a period of time.

examples.sentence: 医生先让他把工作放慢一点，因为最近头痛出现的频率越来越高，再这样下去身体很难受得住。
这台机器虽然还能用，可是出问题的频率比以前高了很多，所以老板已经开始考虑是不是该换新的。
两个人联系的频率一低下来，并不一定代表感情变了，有时候只是生活一下变得太忙。

example_translations.translation: The doctor first told him to slow down his work a little, because the frequency of his headaches has recently become higher and higher, and if it goes on like this, his body will have a hard time enduring it.
Although this machine can still be used, the frequency with which it develops problems is much higher than before, so the boss has already started considering whether a new one should be bought.
If the frequency of contact between two people drops, it does not necessarily mean the relationship has changed; sometimes life has simply suddenly become too busy.

glosses.notes: To taste or sample food carefully, often with attention to flavor and quality.

examples.sentence: 菜刚上来的时候，大家都先不急着说话，而是各自品尝了几口，后来才慢慢开始谈哪个好一点。
老板请我们先品尝新的甜点，不是想让大家马上买，而是想听听第一口吃下去到底是什么感觉。
孩子第一次品尝那种有点苦的茶时先停了一下，可是过了一会儿，反而又想再喝一口试试。

example_translations.translation: When the dishes had just been served, no one hurried to speak first. Instead, each person tasted a few bites, and only later slowly began discussing which was a little better.
The owner invited us to taste the new dessert first, not because he wanted everyone to buy it immediately, but because he wanted to hear what the very first bite really felt like.
When the child tasted that somewhat bitter tea for the first time, he paused for a moment, but after a while he instead wanted to take another sip and try again.

glosses.notes: Equal or equal in standing, treatment, or opportunity rather than necessarily identical in everything.

examples.sentence: 真正的平等不是每个人都拿到一样的东西，而是大家做同样的事时，不会有人还没开始就先被放在后面。
父亲常说，和孩子说话的时候也要有平等的态度，不然你表面上在听，其实心里早就替他决定了。
老师希望大家在讨论时尽量平等一点，因为只有这样，那些平时不太敢说话的人才会真的开口。

example_translations.translation: True equality does not mean that everyone receives exactly the same thing. It means that when people do the same thing, no one is placed behind before even beginning.

My father often says that when speaking with children, you also need an attitude of equality, otherwise on the surface you are listening, but in your heart you have already made the decision for them.
The teacher hopes everyone can be as equal as possible during discussion, because only then will those who are usually less daring to speak truly open their mouths.

glosses.notes: Ordinary, common, or unremarkable in an everyday sense, though not necessarily lacking value.

examples.sentence: 她一直觉得自己的工作很平凡，可是后来很多人才发现，正是这些看上去普通的事每天都不能少。
我最受影响的，不是那些特别出名的人，而是一些生活很平凡却一直认真做事的长辈。
那个故事没有讲什么大人物，只写了几个很平凡的人怎么在小地方把日子慢慢过下去。

example_translations.translation: She always felt that her work was very ordinary, but later many people discovered that it was exactly these seemingly ordinary tasks that could not be missing from each day.
The people who have influenced me most are not those who are especially famous, but rather some elders whose lives are very ordinary yet who have always done things seriously.
That story was not about any great figures, but about how a few very ordinary people slowly carried on with life in a small place.

glosses.notes: Square, often used in mathematics for squaring a number or talking about area in square units.

examples.sentence: 这个数如果再平方一次，结果就会一下大很多，所以老师提醒我们做题的时候不要把顺序看错。
孩子刚学到平方的时候，总觉得这个词听上去很难，后来拿最简单的数字一算，才觉得没有想的那么远。
设计房间时只会看长和宽还不够，因为最后要算出多少平方，才能知道东西放进去以后是不是太挤。

example_translations.translation: If this number is squared one more time, the result becomes much larger all at once, so the teacher reminds us not to read the order wrong when doing problems.

When the child had just learned about squaring, he always felt the word sounded very difficult. Later, after calculating with the simplest numbers, he felt that it was not as distant as he had imagined.

When designing a room, looking only at the length and width is not enough, because in the end you have to calculate how many square units there are before you can know whether things will feel too crowded once they are placed inside.

glosses.notes: Square meter, the standard measure used for room size, floor area, and similar spaces.

examples.sentence: 这个房子虽然只有六十平方米，可是因为窗大、东西也放得很整齐，所以一家人住着并不觉得太小。
老板把那间不到二十平方米的小店慢慢做起来以后，很多人都说，真正让人再来的不是地方大，而是东西做得认真。
学校新开的阅读室有一百多平方米，孩子们一进去就先分开坐好，因为谁都怕自己说话太大影响别人。

example_translations.translation: Although this home is only sixty square meters, because the windows are large and the things are arranged neatly, the whole family does not actually feel it is too small to live in.

After the owner slowly built up that small shop of less than twenty square meters, many people said that what truly made people come again was not that the place was large, but that things were made seriously.

The new reading room opened by the school has more than one hundred square meters. As soon as the children go in, they first sit separately, because everyone is afraid that speaking too loudly will affect others.
